title: Make the product cache's byte budget match the heap

blocks.text: The storefront keeps product descriptions in an in-memory cache with a budget of bytes for their text, so it can't take more than its share of the heap. Its weigher counts each string's UTF-8 size. The caches of the Nordic and the Japanese shops hold fewer products than their budgets allow, while the Dutch shop's, whose descriptions carry prices in euros, takes more than its share of the heap.
Eviction already works. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ProductCache.java`:

items: `textBytes(s)`: how many bytes the characters of `s` take in the heap of a JVM with default settings, leaving out the object's and the array's headers.

cases.says: plain ASCII entries are counted at their length, and the oldest entry is dropped when the budget is passed
a description with Danish letters is counted at one byte per character
a description with one euro sign is counted at two bytes for every character
a Japanese description is counted at two bytes per character, not at its UTF-8 size

origin.section: A String Keeps Latin-1 Text at One Byte per Character, and One Character Beyond Latin-1 Doubles It

concepts: A String stores its characters in Latin-1 at one byte each when all of them are at most U+00FF, and otherwise in UTF-16 at two bytes each, for the whole string.
